outcomes.description: Paper is stuffed into the cup.
outcomes.target: The paper is visibly placed inside the cup, with evidence that it has been stuffed into it rather than merely resting nearby or on its rim.
outcomes.reference: The requested edit is stated in the instruction: “Stuffing the paper into the cup”.

nodes.question: Can the edited scene be visually inventoried to locate the paper and candidate receiving object and describe their visible boundaries and occlusions for a narrower insertion investigation?
nodes.criteria: Pass if visible evidence permits a grounded inventory of the paper and candidate receiving object, including concrete boundaries, visible identifying features, overlap, and visibility limitations. A pass establishes inspectable context only, not confirmed cup identity or insertion. Report separately whether paper identity and cup identity are established, disproved, or unresolved. Fail if adequate visibility positively establishes absence of the paper or any relevant receiving object; identify the decisive evidence. Unknown if framing or visibility prevents even a grounded inventory. Unresolved cup identity must be recorded explicitly and never silently promoted to confirmed identity.
nodes.binding: Inspect source and edit directly. Use the source only to locate the requested objects and compare appearances, not to certify the reddish object's identity. Describe the paper outline and the reddish object's exposed contour and dark marking; investigate whether these support a cup, another object, or neither determination. Consider the combined visible structure without demanding a visible interior as an absolute identity requirement. Distinguish image-plane overlap from entry into a container. Do not infer hidden geometry or stuffing from the hand's grip.

nodes.question: Within the scene inventoried by s1, does direct inspection establish actual paper entry into a cup or an intermediate stuffing action, rather than projected overlap with the reddish object?
nodes.criteria: Pass if the paper and a cup are established by concrete visible features and the paper visibly enters or occupies its interior, or visible deformation and crossing of its opening establish an intermediate stuffing action. Describe the boundary crossing, containment, and whether progress is complete or intermediate; do not infer motion from a grip. Fail only if adequate evidence establishes no requested insertion progress: the paper is wholly external to an identified cup with no entry or stuffing action, contact is demonstrably rim-only, or a required object is positively shown absent. A candidate positively identified as a non-cup can support failure only when the relevant scene is sufficiently visible to exclude another receiving cup or hidden insertion. Unknown if identity, paper boundaries, opening, or occlusion prevents distinguishing entry from overlap. Lack of a visible opening alone is not evidence of no progress.
nodes.binding: Use s1 as coarse ancestor context, including its explicitly unresolved identity fields, and inspect the edited image independently. Examine the exposed reddish contour, dark line, paper edges, and any observable receiving opening, depth, enclosing wall, or boundary crossing. Test cup and non-container interpretations against visible features rather than the instruction. Paper in front of a rounded form, color changes, and hand presence are not insertion evidence. Retain uncertainty if the paper could hide the decisive structure.

nodes.question: Given the visual inventory and direct opening-entry investigation, does the edited image establish completed stuffing of the paper into a cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass if concrete evidence identifies paper and a cup and shows the paper extending inside it with visible containment, compression, or insertion sufficient to establish stuffing. Fail if adequate visual evidence positively establishes the full target is not met, including incomplete insertion, wholly external paper, rim-only placement, or adequately visible absence of a required object. Report whether failure coexists with actual insertion progress or with no progress, without treating completion failure as proof of either. Unknown if identity, containment, or the distinction between completed stuffing and an intermediate state remains unresolved. Some paper may remain outside a successfully stuffed cup.
nodes.binding: Use s1 and s4_opening_entry as ancestor context, then inspect the edited image directly for completed stuffing. Do not treat s1's inventory pass as confirmed cup identity or s4's progress pass as completion. Cite the decisive containment or compression cues and reconcile any disagreement with ancestor observations using visible evidence. Do not infer an interior hidden behind the sheet, require preservation of the source cup's color, or count unrelated changes as progress.

nodes.question: Does the image show the paper stuffed inside the cup?
nodes.criteria: Use all and only s1, s4_opening_entry, and s2 observations in that order. Complete requires grounded paper-and-cup identity, actual insertion evidence from s4_opening_entry, and affirmative contained stuffing evidence from s2. Partial requires positively established insertion or intermediate stuffing progress from s4_opening_entry and positively established incompleteness from s2. Absent requires s4_opening_entry to establish no requested progress using trustworthy external-placement evidence or adequately visible absence of a required object. Failure of s2 alone never establishes absent. Unknown applies when required identity, progress, or completion evidence remains unresolved, or observations conflict without a grounded resolution. A pass on s1 supplies inventory context only; supporting agreement is dependent, not independent confirmation. Do not infer new visual facts.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

s4_opening_entry: The node is over-cautious in a way that misses visible negative evidence. In the edited image, the reddish object is a basketball-like sphere: its curved outer contour and dark seam are visible, with no cup rim, opening, or enclosing interior. The paper lies in front of it; there is no visible entry or stuffing action. Since the scene is sufficiently visible to identify the candidate as non-cup and exclude a hidden receiving cup, the criteria permit `fail` rather than `unknown`. Refine the binding to distinguish genuine occlusion of decisive evidence from a visible, incompatible object and a clearly external paper position; do not treat any obscured area as automatically unresolved. Keep the pass threshold tied to observable entry/deformation, and do not infer progress from overlap or the hand’s grip. The repeated high-confidence unknowns are semantic calibration signals, not transport or dependency failures; s1 and s4 executed validly, and s1’s unresolved identity should inform but not override independent inspection. The reference label is aggregate guidance, not atomic proof, so ground the decision in these visible features rather than forcing a label.
s1: The node is valid and its inventory role is appropriate, but its binding leaves the key negative-evidence decision too open-ended: repeated high-confidence `unresolved` judgments treat the partly occluded object as unidentified despite visible evidence. In the edited image, the exposed reddish object has a rounded ball-like contour and a dark curved seam; the paper is visibly in front of it, with no observable opening, entry, or stuffing. Refine the binding to assess whether the visible features positively support a non-container object and whether the paper is clearly external, rather than treating any occlusion or lack of a visible interior as sufficient for uncertainty. Keep genuine occlusion of decisive features unresolved, and do not infer completion or progress from overlap or the hand’s grip. This is a semantic calibration issue, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure. Use the reference label only as aggregate guidance; ground the decision in the image evidence and preserve the distinction between inventory and insertion.

observations.evidence: The edited scene is clear enough to inventory. The paper is a blue-and-white printed sheet with a roughly rectangular outline, held by a hand; its lower and side edges are visible, while the hand covers part of its upper-left area. A reddish rounded object is partly exposed behind the paper on the right, with a curved outer contour and a dark line across it. The paper overlaps the object in the image plane, but the visible evidence does not establish that the object is a cup or that the paper enters it. Paper identity: established. Cup identity: unresolved; the exposed contour and marking are insufficient to distinguish a cup from another object.

The paper is visibly held in front of a reddish rounded object, but the exposed contour and dark line do not establish a cup opening or interior. The paper’s edge appears to overlap the object in the image plane; no boundary crossing or containment is visible. The paper obscures the decisive area, so insertion progress cannot be distinguished from projected overlap.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The support checks do not provide sufficient evidence to distinguish partial progress from no progress. Both focus on whether the paper is already stuffed inside the cup; s1 treats paper not inside as fail, and s2 only resolves whether the target is complete. The fulfillment readout therefore cannot reliably identify cases where the paper has progressed toward the cup but is not yet stuffed inside. Its absent/partial rules require that distinction, so the saved evidence does not support the requested extent.

findings.source_phrase: Stuffing the paper into the cup
findings.question: On direct inspection of the source and edited images, does the reddish object in the edit correspond to the blue cup in the source, and does its visible shape/marking establish a cup opening or interior despite the paper occlusion?
findings.criteria: Compare concrete visible features across images; distinguish a cup from another rounded object without relying on color alone.
